blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: The City describes Webster's Corners as near the border of Maple Ridge and Mission, just off Dewdney Trunk Road, with a network of mountain-bike trails in the BCIT Woodlot and an active film-production hub.
Nearby areas: Thornhill to the northwest, Whonnock and Ruskin to the east and southeast, Albion to the west, and the City of Mission across the eastern municipal boundary.
There is no West Coast Express station in this sub-area.

Zoning base: the zoning schedule in Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 lists minimum lot areas of RS-2 0.4 ha, RS-3 0.8 ha or 2.0 ha depending on the zone text, A-1 2.0 ha, A-2 4.0 ha and A-3 8.0 ha — the rural zones that cover this area. Rural properties may be on wells and septic — wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained. Confirm any parcel's zone and ALR status per property.

The name itself is spelled two ways. The board and SnapStats write "Websters Corners"; the City and the school district write "Webster's Corners" — searches, school documents and City documents split across the two spellings, and the elementary school's official name carries the apostrophe.

The area doubles as a film set and a trailhead. The City states Webster's Corners is an active hub for film production in Maple Ridge and features the BCIT Woodlot trail network — production traffic and trailhead parking are recurring features of Dewdney Trunk Road life here, not one-offs.

No hospital sits inside the sub-area. The serving facilities are Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, Maple Ridge (24/7 emergency, for Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows), and the Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre at 121 – 11900 Haney Place, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. — both in the Town Centre to the west.

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: The City and school district spell the name with an apostrophe ("Webster's Corners"); the SnapStats row does not. The City describes Webster's Corners as located near the border of Maple Ridge and Mission, just off Dewdney Trunk Road, with a network of mountain-bike trails in the BCIT Woodlot and an active film-production hub.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: nowhere — there is no known townhouse complex and no known apartment-condo building anywhere in this sub-area.

Transit: TransLink route 701 (Coquitlam Central Station / Haney Place / Maple Ridge East / Mission City Station) runs east on Dewdney Trunk Road past this area — most east trips end at Dewdney Trunk Road at 248 Street, and some weekday trips continue non-stop from Haney Place to Mission City Station. There is no West Coast Express station in this sub-area; the nearest stations are Port Haney / Maple Ridge to the west and Mission City to the east.

Zoning base: the area lies outside the Urban Area Boundary and is dominated by RS-2 (minimum lot area 0.4 ha) and RS-3 (0.8 ha or 2.0 ha, per the zone text) with Agricultural Land Reserve parcels; Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 also lists A-1 at 2.0 ha, A-2 at 4.0 ha and A-3 at 8.0 ha. Rural properties may be on wells and septic — wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained. Confirm any parcel's zone and ALR status per property.

Form B diligence (strata townhomes generally): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. No Form B exists for a Websters Corners acreage house — if a listing here claims strata documents, that is a classification error to resolve before subjects.
Lougheed Transit Corridor: It does not designate Websters Corners parcels.

This is the one Maple Ridge sub-area where "townhomes" is an empty search by design. Zero attached listings and zero attached sales in September 2026 is the published position, not a data gap — the sub-area sits outside the Urban Area Boundary on RS-2/RS-3 and agricultural zoning, so strata product has no base here today.

No hospital, recreation centre, library branch or shopping centre sits inside the sub-area. The serving facilities are Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, Maple Ridge (24/7 emergency, for Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows), and the Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre at 121 – 11900 Haney Place, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre (11925 Haney Place), Maple Ridge Public Library (130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road) and Town Centre shopping centred on Haney Place Mall, 11900 Haney Place, are all to the west.

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Main roads and commute: Dewdney Trunk Road is the main east–west road; 248, 256 and 264 Streets run north–south; 128 Avenue runs east–west on the north side.

Schools physically in the area (Ministry-listed names/addresses only): Webster's Corners Elementary, 25554 Dewdney Trunk Road; Blue Mountain Elementary, 12453 248 Street; Garibaldi Secondary, 24789 Dewdney Trunk Road. SD42 has no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12). That chain is documented for that one address only and is non-transferable.

Recreation and services: the BCIT Woodlot trail network and the City's film-production note (above); Kanaka Creek Regional Park at the west side; Whonnock Lake Park in Whonnock to the east. No recreation centre or library branch inside this sub-area — Maple Ridge Leisure Centre, 11925 Haney Place, and Maple Ridge Public Library, 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, are in the Town Centre. Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street (24/7 emergency); Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 121 – 11900 Haney Place, 7 days, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

Lougheed Transit Corridor — adopted Jan 27, 2026 (City record), far west of this area: OCP Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021 was given third reading and adopted Jan 27, 2026 (City news release Feb 4, 2026); the corridor runs from the City's western boundary to the Town Centre at 221 Street — it does not reach Websters Corners, and no lot here is priced on it.

ALR block — full form (Websters Corners farm ground): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)). Residence caps: one principal residence per parcel, maximum 500 m²; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; one additional residence capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. Farm class (BC Assessment) in full three-tier form: $2,500 of gross farm income at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha above that; $10,000 under 0.8 ha — applications by October 31.

The name itself is spelled two ways, and both are official. The City and the school district write "Webster's Corners" with an apostrophe; the board/SnapStats row writes "Websters Corners" without one. A search using only one spelling can miss records filed under the other.
The film industry is part of this area's economy, per the City. The City states Webster's Corners is an active hub for film production in Maple Ridge alongside the BCIT Woodlot trail network.

Most eastbound buses on the main road stop short of here. On route 701, most east trips end at Dewdney Trunk Road at 248 Street; only some weekday trips continue non-stop from Haney Place to Mission City Station — an acreage buyer here is driving, and there is no West Coast Express station in the sub-area.

Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Identity: "Websters Corners" is both a City of Maple Ridge neighbourhood name and the board sub-area name — a clean match.

Main roads: Dewdney Trunk Road east–west; 248 Street, 256 Street and 264 Street north–south; 128 Avenue east–west on the north side. Nearby: Thornhill northwest, Whonnock and Ruskin east/southeast, Albion west, Mission across the eastern municipal boundary.
SD42 has no middle tier — elementary K–7, secondary 8–12.

Transit and services: TransLink route 701 runs east on Dewdney Trunk Road past this area — most east trips end at Dewdney Trunk Road at 248 Street, and some weekday trips continue non-stop from Haney Place to Mission City Station; that claim rests on route 701's own timetable document. There is no West Coast Express station in this sub-area; no City recreation centre or library branch sits inside it (Maple Ridge Leisure Centre, 11925 Haney Place, and Maple Ridge Public Library, 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, are in Town Centre to the west).

Plans: the North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan — Council approved the OCP amendments creating a plan area on both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue (about 500 acres, per the City release); the plan establishes future designations and does not itself approve construction. Council adopted updates to the Official Community Plan on November 25, 2025, and the Albion Area Plan update on October 28, 2025.

Webster's Corners Park is at 25496 Dewdney Trunk Road, next to Webster's Corners Elementary School — the Dewdney Trunk Road address that anchors the community.
The North 256 Street study area description places Webster's Corners south of the Alouette Valley bench, at elevations mainly between 60 and 160 metres above sea level in that study's geography.
Websters Corners is a rural east Maple Ridge community, not a Town Centre housing area: the City's named features for it are trails and film production, not shops or strata complexes.
The community's built anchor is small and specific: a 1.267-hectare neighbourhood park beside the elementary school on Dewdney Trunk Road, rather than a commercial centre.

blocks.text: Websters Corners: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Large-lot and farm rules are parcel-specific in Websters Corners: the City's suite summary lists Agricultural (A-1, A-2, A-3) zones among zones where a secondary suite is permitted under Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, subject to the one-suite and 40% Gross Floor Area limits.

Kanaka Creek watershed rules matter here: the North 256 Street environmental assessment states the southeast portion of that study area, north of Websters Corners, is part of the Kanaka Creek watershed, with tributaries to North Kanaka Creek.
A suite must remain under the same legal title and cannot be a short-term or vacation rental — a limit that applies to a Websters Corners acreage suite as well.

blocks.text: Websters Corners: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Webster's Corners Park is 1.267 hectares and lists drinking water, a fitness circuit, open green space, playground, parking and washrooms on the City's facility page.
The park page was last updated October 24, 2024 on the City site facility status before relying on an amenity list.

The British Columbia Institute of Technology Woodlot trail network is the mountain-bike feature the City names for Webster's Corners — trail access is through the Woodlot, not through the neighbourhood park.
Flood-hazard creeks named in the North 256 Street assessment for the area north of Websters Corners include Mudd, Sawdust, Websters and North Kanaka Creeks, plus the Alouette River floodplain.

Aquifer No. 38 underlies the western side of that northern study area and is recharged from the Alouette River — groundwater is a documented feature of the wider Websters Corners / 256 Street geography.

blocks.text: Websters Corners: development and new projects

items.t: The North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan is the major plan touching the area north of Websters Corners: about 744 hectares north of 128 Avenue / 130 Avenue along 256 Street, south of Alouette Lake, east of Golden Ears Provincial Park and west of Blue Mountain.
Websters Corners is in the City of Maple Ridge, listed by the Province as a Speculation and Vacancy Tax (SVT) taxable area — the Mission border does not change the tax municipality.

Websters Corners has no rapid transit station: its transit connection is by road west on Dewdney Trunk Road to Haney Place Exchange for the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus and to Port Haney / Maple Meadows West Coast Express stations.

blocks.text: Websters Corners: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check creek flood hazard first: the City-commissioned assessment identifies flood-hazard areas along Mudd, Sawdust, Websters and North Kanaka Creeks and in low-lying areas along the southern boundary of the northern study area.

Groundwater and springs are a documented risk factor north of Websters Corners: where ground drops sharply to the Alouette River floodplain, springs feeding small creeks are common, per the same assessment.
The City monitors Kanaka Creek during high streamflow events and maintains dikes and pump stations — a Websters Corners buyer near Kanaka Creek should read MapleRidge.ca/Flood for the specific lot.

faq.q: How did Websters Corners sell in September 2026?

faq.a: One secondary suite per lot is permitted in listed zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3 if it sits inside the single detached building, is at most 40% of gross floor area and is not in the Floodplain Area; on ALR land the ALR Use Regulation also applies, and an additional separate residence is allowed only under its s. 32 conditions — and ALR residences cannot be stratified in any case.
faq.q: Can an acreage home here add a suite or a second dwelling?

faq.a: The North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan, approved by Council as OCP amendments, covers both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue (about 500 acres) at the area's northwest side; it sets future designations and does not itself approve construction — disclose it as a designation change, not a development approval.
faq.q: What major plan affects this area?

faq.a: On the documented base: the sub-area sits outside the Urban Area Boundary on RS-2 / RS-3 and agricultural zoning (minimum lots from 0.4 ha up to 8.0 ha in the A-3 tier), and ALR residences cannot be stratified — strata townhouse product has no zoning or tenure base here today. Confirm any individual parcel's zone and ALR status per property.
faq.q: Why is there no townhouse stock here at all?

faq.a: Treat it as a classification error to resolve before subjects: there is no known strata in this sub-area, an acreage house has no Form B, and the diligence that applies is title, zoning, ALR status, well records (GWELLS) and septic compliance.
faq.q: A listing here says "townhouse-style" / claims strata documents — what do I do?

faq.a: Only one chain is settled, on a single-address basis: 25554 Dewdney Trunk Road → Webster's Corners Elementary / Garibaldi Secondary.
faq.q: Which schools serve my Websters Corners address?

faq.a: The Lougheed corridor ends at 221 St and does not reach this area. The North 256 Street plan changes future designations north of 128 Avenue without approving construction — disclose it as a designation change, not a development approval.
faq.q: Does the Lougheed corridor or the 256 Street plan change my parcel?

faq.a: Webster's Corners Elementary (Kindergarten to grade 7) is at 25554 Dewdney Trunk Road on the provincial School District 42 list. Webster's Corners Park, at 25496 Dewdney Trunk Road, sits next to the school, so school and park traffic share the same Dewdney Trunk Road frontage.
faq.q: Which elementary school is in Websters Corners?

faq.a: Because the City itself calls Webster's Corners an active hub for film production in Maple Ridge, alongside its British Columbia Institute of Technology (BCIT) Woodlot mountain-bike trail network. A buyer should expect occasional production activity and trail-user parking near the Woodlot and Dewdney Trunk Road, rather than a quiet purely farm road at all times.
faq.q: Why do people mention film production in Websters Corners?

faq.a: Kanaka Creek Regional Park flanks both sides of Kanaka Creek for about 11 kilometres from the Fraser River to just south of Websters Corners, and the park hosts the Bell-Irving Hatchery and Kanaka Creek Watershed Stewardship Centre. Creek setbacks and watershed rules are therefore a real check for lots draining toward Kanaka Creek.
faq.q: What is the Kanaka Creek connection?

faq.a: It is near the Maple Ridge–Mission border just off Dewdney Trunk Road, per the City, but it remains a City of Maple Ridge community in School District 42 — not a Mission community in School District 75. A buyer should not assume Mission schools, Mission taxes or Mission utilities apply to a Websters Corners address.
